subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw add native core per-agent spend-budget enforcement, or keep budget enforcement in plugins/external provider controls now that pre-run blocking hooks exist?
rationale: This adds new config surface, provider dispatch policy, persistent accounting semantics, and operator UX; automation cannot choose the product boundary or upgrade contract safely.

options.title: Design native core budgets
options.body: Define a default-unlimited core budget contract with reservations, receipts, status/doctor output, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

options.title: Keep enforcement external/plugin-owned
options.body: Document the current plugin hook/provider controls as the supported path and close or narrow this issue to missing plugin APIs only.

options.title: Narrow to cron/job caps first
options.body: Defer general per-agent budgets and handle per-job max-spend fields through the cron-specific trackers.

recommendation.title: Design native core budgets
recommendation.body: Define a default-unlimited core budget contract with reservations, receipts, status/doctor output, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership of the gateway usage and policy surface makes this the best available routing candidate for the product boundary decision.
